Saved stage-2 einsum graphs of the fourth repair round of the LSTM state-consumer fix for LSTM einsum('abc,abc,abc->abc', h, h, c): the reviewer's historical-unmarked replay (the reviewer's historical-unmarked replay) and the round-4 review's saved einsum_graph.yaml. Both carry three in-graph state slots with only two predecessor entries and NO marker (the round-4 dedup bug); the AF builder must refuse them (state-consumer-p2-6). Hashes in SOURCE.sha256.

Independent reviewer controls for the mixed-boundary findings (state-consumer-p2-7/P2-8), copied verbatim: `round8_mixed_boundary_without_edge.yaml` (a shape-consistent `Boundary` start layer in slot 0, evidenced h_n/c_n in slots 1-2, predecessors `[h_n, c_n]` — the emitter would hand h_n to the boundary slot and invent W3 for c_n), `round8_mixed_boundary_explicit_edge.yaml` (the same with the explicit `Boundary` predecessor entry — exports `[Boundary, h_n, c_n]`), `round8_mixed_boundary_start_slot.yaml` (slot 0 renamed to the graph's own `start.Output`, predecessors `[h_n, c_n]`), `round8_matrix_valid.yaml` / `round8_matrix_permuted.yaml` (two square producers P, Q; consumer `C` names `[P.Output, Q.Output]` with predecessors `[P, Q]` resp. `[Q, P]` — the permutation would export Q @ P), and `round4_lstm_capture_pytorch_graph.yaml` (the round-4 LSTM `einsum('abc,abc,abc->abc', h, h, c)` stage-1 capture the reviewer's three "converter-unmarked" fault cases convert with one predecessor entry removed after the alignment pass).
